checks.lead: Manuel Ávila Camacho (Spanish pronunciation: [maˈnwel ˈaβila kaˈmatʃo]; 24 April 1897 – 13 October 1955) was a Mexican general and politician who served as the president of Mexico from 1940 to 1946. A participant in the Mexican Revolution, he rose to high rank, and served as chief of staff to his predecessor Lázaro Cárdenas. Known as “El Presidente Caballero” (“The Gentleman President”), his administration marked the transition from military to civilian leadership, moderated the radicalism of the Cárdenas era, ended open anticlericalism, reversed socialist education policies, and aligned Mexico with the Allies during World War II.
